findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on file-not-found, permission denied, or I/O errors
findings.failure_mode: entire program crashes on missing or inaccessible metrics file instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>, use map_err on fs::read_to_string, and define a typed LoadError::Io variant

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is I/O (stdout logging) fused inside the data-parsing map closure
findings.failure_mode: parsing logic has a visible side effect; output becomes polluted with log lines, and the function is no longer pure or testable without capturing stdout
findings.fix: remove println! entirely from the parser; move any logging to the shell layer outside load_metrics, passing results through a Result with typed diagnostics

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value strings
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row aborts the entire batch instead of returning a typed parse error for that row
findings.fix: use map_err with a typed ParseError::InvalidValue variant, and handle the Option from parts.get(1) with map_err returning ParseError::MissingField

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy cast; values 65536+ silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value silently wraps to an incorrect u16, corrupting metric data without any error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::ValueOverflow) after parse, or parse directly as u16 with parts[1].parse::<u16>().map_err(...)

findings.problem: parts[0] uses unchecked indexing on a Vec built from split; a line with no comma produces parts with length 1
findings.failure_mode: index out of bounds panic on any CSV line missing the comma separator
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::InvalidLine) and destructure into (_name, value_str) for the one-separator grammar

findings.problem: parts[1] uses unchecked indexing; a line with only one comma-separated field (empty value) or no comma will panic
findings.failure_mode: index out of bounds panic on malformed input rows with missing second field
findings.fix: use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::MissingValue) or restructure with split_once to guarantee at most two fields with a clear error on extra commas

findings.problem: Record.name is pub String — raw primitive domain state. parse_boundary is violated: raw unvalidated String crosses the parse boundary without a fallible smart constructor, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly
findings.failure_mode: any code can create a Record with an empty, whitespace-only, or otherwise illegal name string, bypassing all validation
findings.fix: define a newtype Name(String) with a private constructor and a smart constructor Name::new(s: &str) -> Result<Name, ParseError> that validates non-empty and character constraints

findings.problem: load_metrics fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing (split/collect/map), and domain construction (Record) in a single function with no boundary separation
findings.failure_mode: cannot test parsing logic without a real file on disk; cannot reuse parsing without triggering filesystem access; violates Data/Calculations/Actions architecture
findings.fix: split into (a) parse_records(lines: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> as pure logic and (b) load_metrics(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> as the shell that reads the file and delegates to (a)

findings.problem: load_metrics returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures surface through panic via unwrap
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish file-not-found from malformed data from value overflow; no recovery or retry logic is possible
findings.fix: define enum LoadError { Io(io::Error), Parse(ParseError) } and enum ParseError { InvalidLine, MissingField, InvalidValue, ValueOverflow } with From<io::Error> for automatic conversion

findings.problem: Vec::new with no try_reserve or line-count cap; unbounded input file causes unbounded memory allocation
findings.failure_mode: an attacker or misconfigured system can supply a gigabyte CSV, causing OOM kill or severe memory pressure
findings.fix: accept a max_items parameter, call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation) after cap validation, and reject lines exceeding the cap with ParseError::TooMany

findings.problem: parts: Vec<String> allocates a Vec of trimmed String copies per line before constructing Record
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary double allocation (Vec<String> then Record::name clone); hot-path allocation budget violated
findings.fix: use split_once to get two &str slices directly, then pass them to Record construction or a builder without intermediate Vec<String>

findings.problem: no benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_metrics throughput or memory characteristics
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify that the function meets latency, throughput, or memory-budget requirements under any workload
findings.fix: add a criterion or custom benchmark measuring lines/sec and bytes-allocated per line across small, medium, and large input files

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_metrics throughput or allocation
no profiler data to identify hot paths in the parsing pipeline
no allocation budget or capacity analysis for unbounded file input
no command evidence (cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo test) was executed — static review only
residual_risk: Static review identified 10 findings (7 BLOCKER, 3 MAJOR, 1 MINOR, 1 MISSING) across panic surfaces, unchecked indexing, lossy casts, hidden I/O, raw primitives, shell leakage, unbounded allocation, and missing error taxonomy. No commands were executed; residual risk includes unverified lint/test compliance and absence of performance evidence. The code must be repaired to return Result types, eliminate all unwrap/panic surfaces, replace split/collect with split_once, add typed error taxonomy, newtype the Name field, cap and try_reserve allocations, and remove the println! before any delivery gate.
